The repo here is empty — there's no `misc` or `utils` folder to inspect, so this must be a hypothetical/planning conversation rather than something to execute directly against this checkout. I'll propose a structure based on your description; you can adjust names to match your actual conventions.

**Proposed layout**

```
scripts/
  migrations/          # one-off migration scripts, ideally dated (2024-03-add-index.js)
config/
  templates/           # config templates
docs/
  compliance/           # archived compliance reports
  meeting-notes/        # old meeting notes (or move to a wiki instead of the repo)
packages/shared/        # or libs/shared, common/ — whatever matches your monorepo convention
  <feature-name>/       # helpers shared by 2+ services, grouped by what they do, not "misc"
```

For the old `utils` folder specifically: rather than one flat replacement folder, split the ~30 files by what they actually do (e.g. `date/`, `validation/`, `http/`, `strings/`) or by which domain uses them. A grab-bag folder tends to regrow the same problem under a new name — the fix is usually smaller, purpose-named folders, not a better catch-all.

**Suggested process**
1. Inventory each file's purpose and last-modified/last-used date (find genuinely dead files — compliance archives and old meeting notes are prime candidates for deletion or moving out of the repo entirely, e.g. into a wiki/drive).
2. Bucket by *who uses it* and *why* (shared library code vs. one-time scripts vs. docs) rather than by vague type.
3. Move in small batches with `git mv` (preserves history) and update imports, verifying tests pass after each batch — this is much safer than one big move.

Since there's no actual `misc`/`utils` content in this checkout, I can't run the inventory or the moves myself. If you paste a file listing (or point me at the real repo), I can turn this into a concrete per-file migration plan.
